title: The first falsehood was bodily presence in the Supper, and from it the flight to ubiquity
pass_a_gloss: Of all, the first falsehood truly was asserting a corporal presence in the Holy Supper; from which at last refuge was taken to this sacred anchor, concerning omnipresence, or ubiquity, really communicated to the human nature, as also omnipotence, and so on, whether by effusion, as the Swabians, or by a certain περιχώρησις / emmeation, as Chemnitz the Brunswick theologian, and so on. By the wiser Hessians, Helmstedt men, Anhaltines, and others, who wanted to found corporal presence not on the personal union or on ubiquity, but on the words of institution: This is my body. Add the places twisted by the Swabians and Saxons, Matthew 28:18; Philippians 2:9; Colossians 2:3, 9, and so on, and whatever else has been defended at length by the Palatine, Anhaltine, Cassel theologians, and so on.
pass_b_english: The first falsehood of them all was asserting a bodily presence in the Holy Supper.

From that they finally fled to this sacred anchor: that omnipresence — or ubiquity — and omnipotence too, and the rest, had been really communicated to the human nature, whether by outpouring, as the Swabians say, or by a kind of περιχώρησις / emmeation, as Chemnitz the Brunswick theologian and others say.
The wiser Hessians, Helmstedt men, Anhaltines, and the rest wanted to ground bodily presence not in the personal union or in ubiquity, but in the institution words: This is my body.

Add the places the Swabians and Saxons twist — Matthew 28:18; Philippians 2:9; Colossians 2:3, 9, and so on — and the rest of what the Palatine, Anhaltine, and Cassel theologians have defended at length.
source_text: Omnium vero primum ψεῦδος fuit, asserenda Praesentia Corporalis in S. Coena; Unde tandem ad sacram hanc anchoram perfugium, de Communicata realiter Nat. Humanae Omnipraesentia, seu Ubiquitate, ut & Omnipotentia, &c. seu per effusionem, ut Suevi, seu per quandam περιχώρησιν Emmeationem, ut Chemnitius Brunswicensis Theologus, &c. Prudentioribus Hassis, Helmstadiensibus, Anhaltinis, aliisque, qui praesentiam Corporalem fundare voluerunt non in Unione Personali, aut Ubiquitate, sed in Verbis Institut. Hoc est Corpus meum. Adde torquenda a Suevis & Saxonibus loca, Matth. XXVIII. 18. Phil. II. 9. Col. II. 3. 9. &c. & quae alia sunt prolixe a Theologis Palatinis, Anhaltinis, Cassellanis, &c. vindicata.
notes: Controv. print pp. 62-63 / PDF ~163-164. Bridge from Controv. X: Omnium vero primum ψεῦδος (corporal presence to ubiquity refuge; Suevi effusion / Chemnitz perichoresis; wiser Hesse-Helmstedt-Anhalt on institution words; twisted loci). Controv. XI Q.II follows.
